title: Dark Venture - Review and Give Away
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e83i1spluHo

Fifteen months after the Kickstarter preview, Daniel (@dungeondive) returns with a full verdict — and a copy of the game plus its Vile Invaders expansion to give away, both supplied by designer Robert Lemon, who also drew the Dungeon Dive clipboard logo.

He opens by reading the Cataclysm text aloud, because the world is the argument: two waves of arcane magic breaking over the land, altering every living thing they touch. Everyone in the art looks wrong. "Grotesque" is the word he settles on, and it is a compliment — this took his 2019 award for best art.

Mechanically it remains a competitive overland crawl where the players populate the map. You play the locations, you play the enemies, and in a competitive game you place enemies specifically to wall opponents off from the quest sites they need. Enemies are built identically to heroes, which makes every new arrival a small setup ritual: find the card, find its gear, track its health. The pace is glacial, and Daniel argues that is the design rather than a defect.

His complaints are precise. The rulebook is charming and too small — there is a twelve-page errata PDF on BoardGameGeek doing work the book should have done. There is exactly one helmet in the entire item deck. And his own house solo rules, adopted semi-officially by Lemon, exist purely to fill the world faster.

----

Daniel's house solo rules were good enough that the designer adopted them. When has a house rule improved a game more than an official fix would have?
